ai_evidence.text: Endoscopists’ adenoma detection rate in colonoscopies without AI fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after routine exposure to AI (1,443 patients)
Outside the frontier of what AI does well, knowledge workers using it were correct about 19 percentage points less often; inside it they completed 12.2% more tasks
Knowledge workers with more confidence in AI reported less critical thinking (319 workers)
Automation bias affects experts as well as novices, and training does not remove it
Operators who only monitor automation lose the skill to take over when it fails

Three risks for learners: deskilling, the loss of previously acquired skills; mis-skilling, the reinforcement of incorrect behavior due to AI errors or bias; never-skilling, the failure to develop essential competencies
Students using ChatGPT improved essay scores without more knowledge gain or transfer
AI raised productivity by 15% on average and by 30% for less skilled and less experienced workers
Intelligent tutoring systems raise test performance by a median .66 standard deviations across 50 evaluations
A tutor designed to give one step at a time rather than the full solution doubled learning gains in less time in a randomized crossover trial (median 49 minutes against a 60-minute class)
Open access to GPT-4 raised practice grades by 48% but lowered grades on an exam taken without AI by 17%; a tutor that gave teacher-designed hints removed that loss
ChatGPT produced construction schedules that were coherent but contained wrong tasks
Model-based estimating still leaves the estimator substantial work
Junior employment fell about 9% at firms adopting generative AI, through fewer hires (working paper)
